import java.util.Map;

/**
 * The pinned city-to-region table used to derive an owner's locality. Maps a city to its
 * canonical region; any city not in the table resolves to {@link #UNKNOWN}.
 */
public final class Locality {

    /** Region returned for a city that is not in the {@link #CITY_REGION} table. */
    public static final String UNKNOWN = "UNKNOWN";

    private static final Map<String, String> CITY_REGION = Map.of(

    }

     * @return the region string, or {@link #UNKNOWN} when the city is not in the table.
     */
    public static String forCity(String city) {
        return CITY_REGION.getOrDefault(city, UNKNOWN);
    }
}

components:

    ProblemDetail:

        title:

          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status

          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time

      required:
        - type

      title: Validation message

      required:

      required:

      type: object

        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; stored lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner registered. Optional; defaults to the server's current date when omitted.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'

          title: Shares household
          description: >-

            and address (i.e. they share a household). Request-only directive; not stored.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false

        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: Server-assigned code formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' - the upper-cased first three letters of the last name and a 4-digit global sequence.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: Derived from the owner's own fields, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>' where YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007-M26'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: Stable identifier shared by every owner in the same household (same last name and address). Assigned when an owner is created with sharesHousehold true.
              type: string
              example: 'HH-1A2B3C4D5E6F'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                Derived duplicate-detection key formatted 'normalizedTelephone|email|householdId'
                (telephone in E.164, email lower-cased, each component empty when absent). Two
                owners are duplicates only when their whole identityKey is equal.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678|george.franklin@example.com|HH-1A2B3C4D5E6F'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: The number of existing owners that, at the moment this owner was created, already shared the same firstName and lastName (compared case-insensitively).
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                Derived from the owner's own fields - starts at 1; add 1 when an email is present;
                add 1 when the owner has no namesakes (namesakeCount is 0); capped at 3. Level 4 is
                reserved for tenure.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The canonical region derived from the owner's city using the fixed
                city-to-region table (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD),
                or 'UNKNOWN' when the city is not in the table.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference

              type: string
              example: 'EMAIL'
              readOnly: true

            pets:

          required:

All tests pass and the build succeeds. `AcceptanceTest` is the only concrete test class (`AcceptanceBase` is abstract, `AuditLogCapture` is a helper).

## Summary

I implemented optional, region-validated `postcode` support for owners, keeping each piece in a small single-responsibility unit and reusing the existing city→region table.

**Domain / data**
- `openapi.yml` — added `postcode` to the `OwnerFields` schema (optional, `^[0-9]{4}$`), so the generated DTOs carry it and the response includes it.
- `Owner.java` — added the `postcode` field, `@Column`, accessors, and a backstop `@Pattern` mirroring the existing `telephone` convention.
- `PostcodeRange.java` (new model) — the pinned region→range table (NSW 2000‑2099, VIC 3000‑3099, QLD 4000‑4099), reusing `Locality.forCity(...)` for the city→region lookup; unknown region accepts any 4-digit postcode.
- Added the `postcode` column to all four DB schemas (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres).

**Request handling (OfficeFloor functions)**
- `RequirePostcodeInRegion.java` (new step) — validates *only when present*: rejects malformed (not 4 digits) or out-of-range postcodes with 400; absent postcode passes through, keeping the contract backward-compatible.
- `InvalidPostcodeException` + `InvalidPostcodeExceptionHandler` + escalation YAML — checked exception → 400 ProblemDetail, following the existing escalation pattern.
- Wired `requirePostcode` into both `owners.POST.yml` (after required-fields) and `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` (after validate).
- `ApplyOwner.java` — now copies `postcode` on update; MapStruct auto-maps it by name for create and response.

Why the format check lives in the function rather than relying on DTO bean-validation: the POST pipeline binds `@RequestBody` without `@Valid`, so the DTO's `@Pattern` isn't enforced there (a malformed value otherwise reached the entity and failed at flush as a 500). The function now guarantees a 400 for both malformed and out-of-range cases.

Full suite: `Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — BUILD SUCCESS.
